answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond in escrow before it may trade. Like a prism splitting one beam into many, a single attacker can split funds across countless fake identities, but each copy must lock its own bond, so the cost scales linearly with the number of fakes. Honest agents recover their bond after a summit of verified trades, while cheaters forfeit theirs to a shared pool. A fake that never trades falls into a canyon of locked capital: it earns nothing while its money sits idle, making mass fakery unprofitable.
